q-154868.name: Question 1
q-154868.worked_solution:
The recursive formula is

$$
{a}_{n+1}={a}_{n}+6
$$

where ${a}_{1}=-3.$

We compute ${a}_{2}$ by substituting $n=1$ into the recursive formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n+1} & ={a}_{n}+6 \\ {a}_{1+1} & ={a}_{1}+6 \\ {a}_{2} & ={a}_{1}+6 \\ {a}_{2} & =(-3)+6 \\ {a}_{2} & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${a}_{2}=3.$

q-214107.name: Question 2
q-214107.worked_solution:
The recursive formula is

$$
{a}_{n+1}=2-5{a}_{n}
$$

where ${a}_{1}=-3.$

We compute ${a}_{2}$ by substituting $n=1$ into the recursive formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n+1} & =2-5{a}_{n} \\ {a}_{1+1} & =2-5{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & =2-5{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & =2-5(-3) \\ {a}_{2} & =17\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${a}_{2}=17.$

q-154915.name: Question 3
q-154915.worked_solution:
The recursive formula is

$$
{a}_{n+1}={a}_{n}-3,
$$

where ${a}_{1}=-1.$

We use this formula to compute the terms ${a}_{2}$ and ${a}_{3}$ as follows:

- We first compute ${a}_{2}$ by substituting $n=1$ into the recursive formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n+1} & ={a}_{n}-3 \\ {a}_{1+1} & ={a}_{1}-3 \\ {a}_{2} & ={a}_{1}-3 \\ {a}_{2} & =(-1)-3 \\ {a}_{2} & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

- Then, we compute ${a}_{3}$ by substituting $n=2$ into the recursive formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n+1} & ={a}_{n}-3 \\ {a}_{2+1} & ={a}_{2}-3 \\ {a}_{3} & ={a}_{2}-3 \\ {a}_{3} & =(-4)-3 \\ {a}_{3} & =-7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${a}_{3}=-7.$

EXPLANATION

The recursive formula is an+1=an−3, where a1=−1.

We use this formula to compute the terms a2 and a3 as follows:

  • We first compute a2 by substituting n=1 into the recursive formula: an+1=an−3a1+1=a1−3a2=a1−3a2=(−1)−3a2=−4

  • Then, we compute a3 by substituting n=2 into the recursive formula: an+1=an−3a2+1=a2−3a3=a2−3a3=(−4)−3a3=−7

Therefore, a3=−7.

q-101303.name: Question 4
q-101303.worked_solution:
The recursive formula is

$$
{a}_{n+1}={a}_{n}+4,
$$

where ${a}_{1}=2.$

We use this formula to compute the terms ${a}_{2}$ and ${a}_{3}$ as follows:

- We first compute ${a}_{2}$ by substituting $n=1$ into the recursive formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n+1} & ={a}_{n}+4 \\ {a}_{1+1} & ={a}_{1}+4 \\ {a}_{2} & ={a}_{1}+4 \\ {a}_{2} & =(2)+4 \\ {a}_{2} & =6\end{aligned}
$$

- Then, we compute ${a}_{3}$ by substituting $n=2$ into the recursive formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n+1} & ={a}_{n}+4 \\ {a}_{2+1} & ={a}_{2}+4 \\ {a}_{3} & ={a}_{2}+4 \\ {a}_{3} & =(6)+4 \\ {a}_{3} & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${a}_{3}=10.$

q-51885.name: Question 5
q-51885.worked_solution:
The recursive formula is

$$
f(n+1)=3f(n),
$$

where $f(1)=-2.$

We use this formula to compute the terms $f(2),f(3),$ and $f(4)$ as follows:

- To compute $f(2),$ we substitute $n=1$ into the recursive formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(n+1) & =3f(n) \\ f(1+1) & =3f(1) \\ f(2) & =3f(1) \\ f(2) & =3(-2) \\ f(2) & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

- To compute $f(3),$ we substitute $n=2$ into the recursive formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(n+1) & =3f(n) \\ f(2+1) & =3f(2) \\ f(3) & =3f(2) \\ f(3) & =3(-6) \\ f(3) & =-18\end{aligned}
$$

- To compute $f(4),$ we substitute $n=3$ into the recursive formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(n+1) & =3f(n) \\ f(3+1) & =3f(3) \\ f(4) & =3f(3) \\ f(4) & =3(-18) \\ f(4) & =-54\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fourth term of the sequence is $f(4)=-54.$

EXPLANATION

The recursive formula is f(n+1)=3f(n), where f(1)=−2.

We use this formula to compute the terms f(2),f(3), and f(4) as follows:

  • To compute f(2), we substitute n=1 into the recursive formula: f(n+1)=3f(n)f(1+1)=3f(1)f(2)=3f(1)f(2)=3(−2)f(2)=−6

  • To compute f(4), we substitute n=3 into the recursive formula: f(n+1)=3f(n)f(3+1)=3f(3)f(4)=3f(3)f(4)=3(−18)f(4)=−54

q-217117.name: Question 6
q-217117.worked_solution:
The recursive formula is

$$
f(n+1)=7-3f(n),
$$

where $f(1)=1.$

We use this formula to compute the terms $f(2)$ and $f(3)$ as follows:

- To compute $f(2),$ we substitute $n=1$ into the recursive formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(n+1) & =7-3f(n) \\ f(1+1) & =7-3f(1) \\ f(2) & =7-3f(1) \\ f(2) & =7-3(1) \\ f(2) & =4\end{aligned}
$$

- To compute $f(3),$ we substitute $n=2$ into the recursive formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(n+1) & =7-3f(n) \\ f(2+1) & =7-3f(2) \\ f(3) & =7-3f(2) \\ f(3) & =7-3(4) \\ f(3) & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(3)=-5.$
